title: Long-term, in toto live imaging of the developing mouse heart
protocol: Euthanize pregnant mice with 4% chloral hydrate.
Soak the abdomen with 70% ethanol, then make an incision at the midline of the abdomen and pull the skin apart.
Cut the peritoneum to expose the abdominal cavity.
Place the uterus into dissection medium after cutting it free from surrounding tissues.
Separate each embryo with forceps between implantation sites.
Peel back the surrounding muscle layer and expose decidua tissue.
Clip off 1/5 portion of the decidua, exposing the embryo.
Dissect out the enveloped decidua with fine forceps.
Remove ectoplacental cone, yolk sac, and amnion with super fine forceps when embryos are later than E8.25.
Transfer the embryos to a Petri dish or agarose tube containing culture medium-V2.
Place the Petri dish or agarose tube in an incubator set at 37°C, 5% CO₂, and 95% air.
Make hollow agarose cylinders by inserting component B into component A filled with 2% low melting-temperature agarose.
Remove component A to form a triangular hollow.
Suck the mouse embryo with culture medium-V2 into the hollow in the agarose holder.
Combine the agarose holder with a base support.
Mount the agarose holder and base on the chamber, fill the chamber with culture medium-V3.
Set up the environment on the microscopy: Open and adjust gas mixer to 5% CO₂, 5% O₂, and 90% N₂.
Pre-heat the chamber to 37°C using a water bath surrounding the chamber.
Image the embryos with a step size of 2.5 μm up to a total of ~400 μm.
Use 3 min intervals for imaging.
Lower laser power and exposure time are used to obtain better results.
